title: The 27 nakshatras and the dasha clock
goal: Done when you can find the nakshatra, pada and D9 sign of any longitude, name each nakshatra’s lord, deity, gana and class from the tables, run tara bala and chandra bala for a given day, and compute a Vimshottari dasha balance by hand and match it to the engine.

gana: The temperament class of a nakshatra: Deva (gentle, god-like), Manushya (human, mixed), Rakshasa (forceful, strongly driven). Rakshasa does not mean evil. Used in matching and in character reading.
yoni: The “animal” assigned to each nakshatra, 14 animals in male and female pairs. It stands for instinct and physical temperament and is used in matching (4 points).
nadi: A three-way classification of the 27 nakshatras: Adi, Madhya, Antya, linked to the humours Vata, Pitta, Kapha. In matching it carries the most points (8).
shakti: The specific power or function given to a nakshatra in the tradition that follows the Taittiriya Brahmana, for example “power to burn” for Krittika.
purushartha: The four aims of life: dharma (duty), artha (wealth and means), kama (desire) and moksha (liberation). Modern tables assign one aim to each nakshatra as its underlying motivation.
muhurta: Choosing a favourable time for an action. Nakshatra class, tara bala and chandra bala are three of its basic filters.
navamsa: The ninth division (D9) of a sign: nine slices of 3°20′ each. Every pada of a nakshatra falls in exactly one navamsa. The D9 chart is read for strength and for marriage.
abhijit: A short 28th nakshatra between Uttara Ashadha and Shravana, used in some muhurta traditions. The Vimshottari dasha and this course use 27 equal nakshatras.
gandanta: “Knot at the end.” The junction where a water sign ends and a fire sign begins, the last part of Ashlesha, Jyeshtha and Revati and the first part of Magha, Mula and Ashwini. Traditionally a sensitive zone for the Moon at birth.
tarabala: A daily check. Count from your birth nakshatra to the day’s Moon nakshatra, divide by 9 and read the remainder as one of nine taras, some good and some bad.
chandrabala: A daily check. The Moon’s transit sign counted from your natal Moon sign: houses 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11 are favourable, 4, 8, 12 unfavourable.
chandrashtama: The Moon transiting the 8th sign from your natal Moon sign, about two and a quarter days each month. The classic day to avoid new starts.
vimshottari: The 120-year dasha system. Nine planets share 120 years in a fixed order; the starting point comes from the Moon’s nakshatra at birth.
mahadasha: The major period of one planet in the Vimshottari system, from 6 to 20 years.
antardasha: A sub-period inside a mahadasha. Each mahadasha splits among all nine planets in proportion to their years.
bhogya: The part of the first mahadasha that remains at birth. It equals the lord’s years multiplied by the fraction of the Moon’s nakshatra still to be crossed.
starlord: The lord of the nakshatra a planet occupies. Many teachers say a planet delivers its results through its star lord as well as its sign lord.

lessons.title: The frame: 27 nakshatras, nine lords, 108 padas
lessons.body:
Recall: What is the ayanamsa, and how do you use it to turn a tropical longitude into a sidereal one?

Stage 1 gave you the 27 nakshatras as a list. This lesson gives you the machinery: how to find the nakshatra and pada for any longitude, and how to read the attributes in the tables that follow.

Why 27, and why 13°20′

The Moon takes about 27.3 days to return to the same star. It moves roughly one mansion a day, so the sky was cut into 27 equal stages. 360° ÷ 27 = 13°20′, which is 800 arcminutes. Each {{term:nakshatra|nakshatra}} splits into four {{term:pada|padas}} of 3°20′ (200′). 27 × 4 = 108 padas.

UnitSizeCount
Zodiac360° = 21,600′1
Sign (rashi)30° = 1,800′12
Nakshatra13°20′ = 800′27
Pada3°20′ = 200′108
Navamsa (D9 slice)3°20′ = 200′108

So a sign holds exactly 2¼ nakshatras, or nine padas. Nine nakshatras (36 padas) fill exactly 120°, which is four signs.

Finding the nakshatra and pada from a longitude

Use the sidereal (Lahiri) longitude, counted from 0° Aries. Convert to a number of degrees (sign number × 30 + degrees in sign).

StepRuleYour Moon
1. Full longitudeSign index × 30 + degrees in sign (Aries = 0)Cancer is sign 3: 3 × 30 + 8°04′ = 98°04′
2. Nakshatra numberDivide by 13°20′ and round up98°04′ ÷ 13°20′ = 7.35, so the 8th: Pushya
3. Start of that nakshatra(number − 1) × 13°20′7 × 13°20′ = 93°20′
4. Distance elapsedLongitude − start98°04′ − 93°20′ = 4°44′ (4°43′47″ unrounded)
5. PadaDivide elapsed by 3°20′ and round up4°44′ ÷ 3°20′ = 1.42, so pada 2

From pada to navamsa sign

The padas are numbered 1 to 108 from the start of Aries and the {{term:navamsa|navamsa}} signs simply run Aries, Taurus, Gemini … Pisces and then repeat. The rule: navamsa sign number = (4 × (nakshatra number − 1) + pada − 1) mod 12, with Aries = 0.

PlacementCalculationNavamsa signEngine D9
Moon, Pushya pada 24 × 7 + 1 = 29, 29 mod 12 = 5VirgoVirgo
Sun, Ardra pada 24 × 5 + 1 = 21, 21 mod 12 = 9CapricornCapricorn
Ketu, Shatabhisha pada 24 × 23 + 1 = 93, 93 mod 12 = 9CapricornCapricorn

Twelve padas (three nakshatras) fill one full circuit of the 12 navamsa signs. So every third nakshatra begins on an Aries navamsa: Ashwini, Rohini, Punarvasu, Magha, Hasta, Vishakha, Mula, Shravana and Purva Bhadrapada. This is why each pada gives you its D9 sign without a separate chart calculation.

The nine lords, three rounds

The lords repeat in the same order three times: Ketu, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury. The sequence is the dasha order too.

LordRound 1Round 2Round 3
KetuAshwiniMaghaMula
VenusBharaniPurva PhalguniPurva Ashadha
SunKrittikaUttara PhalguniUttara Ashadha
MoonRohiniHastaShravana
MarsMrigashiraChitraDhanishta
RahuArdraSwatiShatabhisha
JupiterPunarvasuVishakhaPurva Bhadrapada
SaturnPushyaAnuradhaUttara Bhadrapada
MercuryAshleshaJyeshthaRevati

The attribute key

The next four lessons give each nakshatra a row of attributes. Here is what each one means and where you use it.

AttributeWhat it isUsed for
LordThe planet that rules the nakshatraDasha order; the “channel” through which a planet placed there delivers
Deity and mythThe Vedic god and the story attachedTheme of the nakshatra; rites and mantras
SymbolThe picture in the skyA memory image; hints at the nakshatra’s nature
{{term:shakti|shakti}}The specific power listed in the Taittiriya traditionFlavour of the nakshatra’s action
{{term:gana|gana}}Deva, Manushya or Rakshasa temperamentCharacter; matching (6 points)
{{term:yoni|yoni}}One of 14 animals, in male and female pairsInstinct; matching (4 points)
{{term:nadi|nadi}}Adi, Madhya or Antya (Vata, Pitta, Kapha)Constitution; matching (8 points)
{{term:purushartha|purushartha}}Dharma, artha, kama or mokshaThe underlying motivation
ClassOne of seven muhurta classes (below)Choosing the right time for a task

The seven muhurta classes

ClassNakshatrasSuits
Fixed · DhruvaRohini, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara BhadrapadaFoundations, planting, building, starting a long-term post
Movable · CharaPunarvasu, Swati, Shravana, Dhanishta, ShatabhishaTravel, vehicles, anything that moves
Fierce · UgraBharani, Magha, Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Purva BhadrapadaBold, forceful or destructive acts such as surgery
Mixed · MishraKrittika, VishakhaFire, metal and ordinary work
Light · KshipraAshwini, Pushya, HastaTrade, opening a shop, education, ornaments, arts
Soft · MriduMrigashira, Chitra, Anuradha, RevatiMusic, clothing, friendships, gentle works
Sharp · TikshnaArdra, Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, MulaHard, forceful and tantric work; not for gentle new starts

4 + 5 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 27. Every nakshatra is in exactly one class.

Where the schools differ

27 or 28 nakshatras. Some Vedic texts and muhurta traditions add Abhijit, a short 28th mansion between Uttara Ashadha and Shravana. The Brihat Samhita assigns it to Brahma. The Vimshottari dasha, the matching tables and this course use 27 equal nakshatras, so Abhijit is a muhurta-only extra.

Equal or unequal. Astronomical texts also describe each nakshatra by a junction star (yogatara) at unequal spacings. Jyotish predictions and the dasha use the equal 13°20′ division.

Ayanamsa moves the edges. Raman’s ayanamsa is about 1.4° smaller than Lahiri’s, so every sidereal longitude comes out about 1.4° larger. That is more than a tenth of a nakshatra. A planet within about 1.5° of a nakshatra edge can change nakshatra between systems. This course uses Lahiri throughout.

Cross-check

Do the pada-to-navamsa calculation for your Moon by hand (Virgo), then compare with the D9 column in the engine’s natal output. If they match, you have both the pada boundaries and the D9 rule right. A Moon whose pada is 1 and whose D9 sign comes out differently means you rounded the wrong way in step 5.

In your chart

Your Moon is at Cancer 8°04′, which is 98°04′ from 0° Aries. That is 4°44′ into Pushya (which starts at 93°20′), pada 2, with the Moon’s D9 in Virgo. Your Sun is at Gemini 10°41′ (70°41′): Ardra, pada 2, D9 Capricorn. Your lagna (Virgo 21°52′, which is 171°52′) is in Hasta, pada 4, D9 Cancer. All three agree with the engine.

Remember
  • 360° ÷ 27 = 13°20′ (800′). A pada is 3°20′ (200′). 108 padas in all.
  • Nakshatra number = longitude ÷ 13°20′ rounded up; pada = elapsed ÷ 3°20′ rounded up.
  • Navamsa sign = (4 × (nak − 1) + pada − 1) mod 12, Aries = 0.
  • Lords run Ketu, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, three times.
  • Every nakshatra belongs to one of seven muhurta classes (4, 5, 5, 2, 3, 4, 4).

Practice: find the nakshatra, pada and navamsa sign by hand for your Mars (Taurus 29°19′) and your Jupiter (Pisces 3°28′). Check both against the engine natal output before you read on.
lessons.listen: The zodiac is cut into twenty seven nakshatras of thirteen degrees twenty minutes, which is eight hundred arcminutes. Each has four padas of three degrees twenty minutes, so there are one hundred and eight padas. To find a nakshatra, turn the sidereal longitude into degrees from zero Aries, divide by thirteen twenty, and round up. To find the pada, divide the distance elapsed in that nakshatra by three twenty and round up. The pada also gives the navamsa sign: four times the nakshatra number minus one, plus the pada minus one, taken modulo twelve, with Aries as zero. Your Moon at Cancer eight degrees four minutes is Pushya pada two, navamsa Virgo. The lords repeat Ketu, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury three times. Each nakshatra also carries a gana, a yoni animal, a nadi and one of seven muhurta classes, which the next lessons teach.

Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, chapter on the nakshatras and the Vimshottari lords
Muhurta Chintamani, section on the classes of nakshatras
Drik Panchang, “Seven categories of nakshatra” (modern reference, used to confirm class membership)

quiz.q: How wide is one pada?
quiz.w: 800′ ÷ 4 = 200′ = 3°20′. 13°20′ is the whole nakshatra.

quiz.q: A planet is at Cancer 8°04′ (98°04′). Which nakshatra and pada?
quiz.w: 98°04′ ÷ 13°20′ = 7.35, so the 8th nakshatra (Pushya). It starts at 93°20′, and 4°44′ ÷ 3°20′ = 1.42 puts it in pada 2.

quiz.q: How many nakshatras does one sign hold?
quiz.w: 30° ÷ 13°20′ = 2.25. A sign holds nine padas.

quiz.q: Which three nakshatras share the lord Ketu?
quiz.w: The lord order repeats every 9 nakshatras. Ketu rules Ashwini (1), Magha (10) and Mula (19). Ashlesha, Jyeshtha and Revati are Mercury’s.

quiz.q: A nakshatra in the Fixed (Dhruva) class suits which kind of work?
o: Tantric rites and harsh, secret acts
quiz.w: Fixed nakshatras (Rohini, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada) suit lasting beginnings.

lessons.title: Nakshatras 1–7: Ashwini to Punarvasu
lessons.body:
Recall: Name the nine nakshatra lords in order, and say how a pada gives you its D9 sign.

This lesson covers nakshatras 1 to 7 in zodiac order. Read the tables first, then the stories. The stories are there to make the table stick.

PunarvasuDevaCat (female)Adi (Vata)ArthaMovable (Chara)
NakshatraShakti (power)Favourable for
Ashwinishidhra-vyapani: power to reach things quicklyOpening a shop, selling, starting education, ornaments, arts; Light-class works also suit movable tasks such as travel.
Bharaniapa-bharani: power to take away, to carry offBold, forceful work: surgery, work with fire, buying or selling arms. Not for gentle new starts.
Krittikadahana: power to burnWork with fire and metal, welding, preparing medicines, agnihotra. Ordinary rather than auspicious for new ventures.
Rohinirohana: power of growthFoundations, sowing and planting, building, starting a job, marriage, upanayana, coronation.
Mrigashiraprinana: power to give fulfilmentSinging and learning music, clothing, friendships, ornaments, marriage. Gentle works.
Ardrayatna: power of effortForceful, hard tasks, taming and training animals, hatha yoga and sadhana, tantric work. Poor for gentle new beginnings.
Punarvasuvasutva-prapana: power to regain wealth or substanceTravel, riding vehicles, anything that involves motion.

Shakti names: these are the powers listed under the Taittiriya Brahmana (nakshatra section) with the commentary of Bhatta Bhaskara, as compiled in modern books. This list was compared with one modern compilation. Not verified against the original text: each term in the Sanskrit. Translations of the English meanings vary between authors. Use them as flavour, not as proof.

The purpose column follows the table printed on two modern nakshatra reference sites that agree with each other. Older and regional tables differ in places, and there is no single classical verse that fixes all 27. Tri-guna (sattva, rajas, tamas) assignments differ even more between teachers, so this course leaves them out rather than pick one table.

Padas and their navamsa signs

Each pada is 3°20′, counted from the start of the nakshatra. The signs below are the D9 sign of each pada, from the rule in lesson 3-1.

NakshatraSpanPada 1 navamsaPada 2Pada 3Pada 4
AshwiniAries 0°00′ – 13°20′AriesTaurusGeminiCancer
BharaniAries 13°20′ – 26°40′LeoVirgoLibraScorpio
KrittikaAries 26°40′ – Taurus 10°00′SagittariusCapricornAquariusPisces
RohiniTaurus 10°00′ – 23°20′AriesTaurusGeminiCancer
MrigashiraTaurus 23°20′ – Gemini 6°40′LeoVirgoLibraScorpio
ArdraGemini 6°40′ – 20°00′SagittariusCapricornAquariusPisces
PunarvasuGemini 20°00′ – Cancer 3°20′AriesTaurusGeminiCancer

The nakshatras one by one

1 · Ashwini अश्विनी

The Ashvins are the twin physicians of the gods, riders of a swift chariot who appear at dawn. In the Rig Veda they restore youth to the aged sage Chyavana and rescue the shipwrecked. They are healers first, and they arrive fast.

Reads as: Speed, first-mover energy and a healer’s hands. Starts things, often before the plan is ready. The shadow is impatience: many beginnings, fewer finishes.

2 · Bharani भरणी

Yama, first mortal to die and so lord of the dead, weighs deeds and keeps dharma. In the Katha Upanishad the boy Nachiketa sits three nights at his door and makes him teach what lies beyond death. Bharani is the one who bears the load and carries things across.

Reads as: Intensity with restraint: the capacity to carry heavy responsibility, hold desire and discipline together, and see things through to an end. Extremes of appetite and austerity are both common.

3 · Krittika कृत्तिका

Agni carries the sacrificial offering to the gods. In the Skanda story the six Krittikas, the Pleiades, nurse the infant Kartikeya after Agni bears Shiva’s seed to the Ganga. The fire that purifies and the women who raise a war-god are the same star.

Reads as: A cutting, purifying mind: sharp speech, high standards, a talent for editing out what is false. Authority comes from the Sun’s rulership. The shadow is harshness toward others.

4 · Rohini रोहिणी

Rohini is the favourite of the Moon’s 27 wives, daughters of Daksha. When Chandra lavished his time on her, the others complained and Daksha cursed him to wane. The waning of the Moon is the traditional explanation of that curse.

Reads as: Growth, beauty, magnetism and a love of comfort. Things planted here tend to take root. The shadow is attachment, possessiveness and difficulty letting go.

5 · Mrigashira मृगशिरा

Soma is both the Moon and the sacred plant-drink of the Vedic ritual. In the Aitareya Brahmana story Prajapati takes the form of a stag; the gods make a fierce archer, Rudra, who shoots him. The sky is read as the stag (Mrigashira), the hunter star Mrigavyadha (Sirius) and the arrow.

Reads as: A searcher: curious, gentle, always looking for the next thing. Research, travel and enquiry suit it. The shadow is restlessness that never settles on one answer.

6 · Ardra आर्द्रा

Rudra, “the howler”, is the storm and the hunter, an older form of Shiva whose arrows bring sickness and also healing. Ardra means “moist”: the first rain after a dry spell, tears, the storm that breaks and then clears.

Reads as: Emotional storms followed by clarity. Strong intellect with an edge, drawn to technology, research and breaking old structures. The shadow is destructiveness and mood swings.

7 · Punarvasu पुनर्वसु

Aditi, “the boundless”, is mother of the gods. Punarvasu means “good again”: the arrow returns to the quiver and the traveller returns home. Valmiki places Rama’s birth under Punarvasu.

Reads as: Renewal and return. Optimistic, tolerant, a natural teacher and shelterer. Recovers well after setbacks. The shadow is drifting without settling.

Where the schools differ

Rohini’s deity. The Vedic name is Prajapati. Later books identify Prajapati with Brahma and list Brahma. The Brihat Samhita’s deity table (ch. 98, as in Iyer’s English translation) lists Prajapati for Rohini and Brahma for Abhijit.

Ashwini’s class. Muhurta lists place Ashwini with the Light (Kshipra) nakshatras, as here. Some modern reference tables label it Movable instead. Check which table a panchang uses before comparing.

Symbols. Bharani is a yoni (womb) in most lists. Ardra is a teardrop in most lists, a diamond or a head in some. Punarvasu is a quiver in most lists, a bow or a house in some. Krittika is a razor or a flame. None changes the meaning much, but quizzes and software pick one.

The Moon’s exaltation. Many books say the Moon is exalted “in Rohini”. The exaltation degree is Taurus 3°, which falls in Krittika, pada 2. Rohini is where the tradition places the Moon’s favourite, not its exact exaltation point.

Cross-check

Pick any date and look up the Moon’s nakshatra in two independent Lahiri-based panchangs. They must agree. If they differ by one nakshatra, one of them uses another ayanamsa or the Moon is within a few arcminutes of the boundary. Do the same with the engine: ask for your own natal chart, then check that the nakshatra of each planet matches a free chart you cast elsewhere.

In your chart

Five of your planets sit in this group of seven:

PlanetPlacementStar lordD9 (from the pada)

Your Saturn is debilitated in Aries but sits in Ashwini, the first nakshatra, with Ketu as its lord. Your Mercury in Punarvasu pada 3 has the same sign in D1 and D9 (Gemini), which is the vargottama condition. Both of these are facts from the engine, not readings.

Remember
  • Ashwini, Magha and Mula share the lord Ketu; Bharani, Purva Phalguni and Purva Ashadha share Venus. Learn the sets of three.
  • Ashwini is Deva, Light; Bharani Manushya, Fierce; Krittika Rakshasa, Mixed; Rohini Manushya, Fixed; Mrigashira Deva, Soft; Ardra Manushya, Sharp; Punarvasu Deva, Movable.
  • Rohini, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha and Uttara Bhadrapada are the four Fixed nakshatras.
  • Krittika spans two signs: Aries 26°40′ to Taurus 10°. The Moon’s exaltation degree (Taurus 3°) is in Krittika.

Practice: say the lord, deity and gana of each of your Saturn, Venus, Mars, Sun and Mercury nakshatras from memory, then check against the tables.
lessons.listen: Seven nakshatras from Ashwini to Punarvasu. Ashwini is ruled by Ketu, deity the Ashvins, the divine physicians, symbol a horse’s head, shakti the power to reach quickly. Bharani, ruled by Venus, deity Yama, symbol the womb, bears and carries. Krittika, ruled by the Sun, deity Agni, is the razor and the flame, and spans Aries and Taurus. Rohini, ruled by the Moon, is the growing, fixed nakshatra and the Moon’s favourite wife in the myth. Mrigashira, ruled by Mars, deity Soma, is the deer’s head, the searcher. Ardra, ruled by Rahu, deity Rudra, is the teardrop and the storm. Punarvasu, ruled by Jupiter, deity Aditi, is the quiver and the return. In your chart your Saturn is in Ashwini, your Venus in Krittika, your Mars in Mrigashira, your Sun in Ardra and your Mercury in Punarvasu.

quiz.q: Which nakshatra has Agni as its deity and a razor or flame as its symbol?
quiz.w: Agni is the fire god; Krittika is the razor-or-flame star.

quiz.q: Which nakshatra is both Fixed in class and Manushya in gana?
quiz.w: Rohini is Fixed (Dhruva) and Manushya. Ashwini and Punarvasu are Deva; Mrigashira is Deva and Soft.

quiz.q: Where does the Moon’s exaltation degree (Taurus 3°) actually fall?
quiz.w: Krittika runs from Aries 26°40′ to Taurus 10°. Taurus 3° is in its second pada. Rohini starts at Taurus 10°.

quiz.q: Ardra’s lord is Rahu. Which nakshatra after it has Jupiter as lord?
quiz.w: Order: Ardra (Rahu), Punarvasu (Jupiter), Pushya (Saturn), Ashlesha (Mercury).

quiz.q: Which is the yoni of Mrigashira and Rohini?
quiz.w: Rohini is the male serpent and Mrigashira the female serpent in the Ashtakoota yoni table.

The nakshatras one by one

8 · Pushya पुष्य

Brihaspati is teacher and priest of the gods and “lord of prayer”. The Rig Veda calls this star Tishya, the auspicious one. The udder image is a nourishing, steady supply that asks nothing back.

Reads as: Nourishing and dutiful. Pushya is the most widely praised nakshatra for constructive work. The Saturn lordship adds discipline; the shadow is conservatism and duty carried as burden.

9 · Ashlesha आश्लेषा

The Nagas are the serpent beings of the underworld. Vasuki served as the rope when gods and demons churned the ocean, and Shesha holds the world on his hoods. Ashlesha means “the clinging one”, the embrace that is hard to shake off.

Reads as: Penetrating, strategic, hypnotic. Reads people and situations at depth. The shadow is clinging, secrecy and manipulation. The last part of Ashlesha is a gandanta zone (see below).

10 · Magha मघा

The Pitris live in the world of the ancestors and receive the offerings of their descendants in shraddha. Magha is the throne room of that lineage: authority is inherited and must be honoured.

Reads as: Dignity, lineage, a sense of rank and a pull to honour ancestors. Natural leaders who can become proud. The shadow is entitlement.

11 · Purva Phalguni पूर्वफल्गुनी

Bhaga is the Aditya of fortune and of one’s rightful share. At Daksha’s sacrifice Bhaga lost his eyes, so fortune is said to be “blind” and must be earned by right action.

Reads as: Enjoyment, creativity, romance, rest after effort. Magnetic and pleasure-loving. The shadow is indulgence and a taste for ease.

12 · Uttara Phalguni उत्तरफल्गुनी

Aryaman is the Aditya of hospitality, contracts and marriage alliances, and in the Gita Krishna calls him the chief of the Pitris. He is the patron of agreements made in good faith.

Reads as: Reliable, helpful, a builder of alliances and long-term service. The shadow is over-obligation.

13 · Hasta हस्त

Savitar is the sun as the one who “impels”, to whom the Gayatri mantra is addressed. The Rig Veda gives him golden hands, which is why this star is a hand.

Reads as: Skill of the hands and a quick, practical wit: craft, healing, trade, handling. The shadow is cunning used for small gains.

14 · Chitra चित्रा

Tvashtar is the divine craftsman who fashioned Indra’s thunderbolt and the forms of living things. The tradition often fuses him with Vishvakarma, the architect of the gods.

Reads as: Design, brilliance and the urge to make something beautiful and exact. Charismatic, image-conscious. The shadow is vanity and perfectionism.

Gandanta: the junction after Ashlesha

Ashlesha ends where Cancer ends, and Magha begins where Leo begins. This is a water-to-fire junction, and the Moon or lagna there is called {{term:gandanta|gandanta}}. Traditional texts treat birth in this junction as a sensitive start. Commonly it is taken as the last pada of Ashlesha and the first pada of Magha (3°20′ on each side).

Where the schools differ

The two Phalgunis. The Taittiriya Brahmana’s Nakshatra Suktam gives Aryaman to Purva Phalguni and Bhaga to Uttara Phalguni. The Brihat Samhita and most Jyotish books reverse this: Bhaga for Purva, Aryaman for Uttara. This lesson follows the Jyotish books. Both are classical, so know which one a teacher uses.

Chitra’s deity. Most Jyotish tables list Tvashtar. Some reference sites list Vishvakarma. In the tradition the two are often merged as the divine craftsman.

Uttara Phalguni and marriage. It is in the standard list of marriage nakshatras, yet some astrologers avoid it for weddings because of the story of Rama and Sita. This is a lineage choice.

Gandanta width. Commonly one pada on each side of the junction. Some authorities use a much narrower band at the exact junction. Treat the wider band as the caution zone.

Cross-check

A Moon in the last pada of Ashlesha (Cancer 26°40′–30°) or the first of Magha (Leo 0°–3°20′) is within the gandanta band. If your birth time is uncertain, move it by ±5 minutes: the Moon travels about 0.05° in that time, so you only need to worry when the Moon is within a few arcminutes of the junction itself. Your Moon is nowhere near one.

In your chart

Your Moon is in Pushya, pada 2, at Cancer 8°04′ (D9 Virgo). Pushya is Light class, Deva gana, Madhya nadi, Saturn’s star with Brihaspati as deity. Your lagna, Virgo 21°52′, is in Hasta pada 4 (D9 Cancer). Your Rahu, Leo 10°33′, is in Magha pada 4 (D9 Cancer), so your lagna and Rahu share a D9 sign.

That gives you three of your most important points in this one lesson: the Moon (mind), the lagna (body) and Rahu (the hungry node). Their star lords are Saturn (for the Moon), the Moon (for the lagna) and Ketu (for Rahu).

Remember
  • Pushya is the most widely praised nakshatra for constructive work, but it is not used for marriage (the sources consulted agree).
  • Magha, Purva Phalguni: Fierce class. Uttara Phalguni: Fixed. Hasta: Light. Chitra: Soft. Ashlesha: Sharp. Pushya: Light.
  • The Phalguni deities are swapped between the Taittiriya Brahmana and the Brihat Samhita. Know which one your source uses.
  • Ashlesha to Magha is the first gandanta junction (Cancer to Leo).

Ashlesha, ruled by Mercury, deity the Nagas, is the coiled serpent and a Sharp nakshatra. Magha, ruled by Ketu, deity the Pitris, is the throne. The nakshatras one by one

15 · Swati स्वाति

Vayu is the wind, father of Hanuman and, by his gift, of Bhima. He is independent, restless and everywhere, as the shoot bends but does not break.

Reads as: Independence, flexibility and a talent for trade and diplomacy. The shadow is scattering, being blown by every wind.

16 · Vishakha विशाखा

Indra and Agni are the king of the gods and the fire, invoked together in the Rig Veda as partners who win battles. Skanda is also called Vishakha in the epics.

Reads as: Goal-driven, persistent, ambitious and ready to compete. The shadow is single-minded rivalry and jealousy.

17 · Anuradha अनुराधा

Mitra is the Aditya of friendship, oaths and agreements, partner of Varuna. Anuradha means “following Radha”, success that comes by devotion and loyalty.

Reads as: Friendship, organisation and devotion. Does well far from home. The shadow is over-work and withheld feeling.

18 · Jyeshtha ज्येष्ठा

Indra, king of the gods, slayer of the serpent Vritra, holds the “eldest” (jyeshtha) rank. The myths show him powerful and insecure about it in equal measure.

Reads as: Seniority, protectiveness and a need for status. Capable under pressure. The shadow is rivalry and fear of losing rank.

19 · Mula मूल

Nirriti is the goddess of dissolution and misfortune, honoured so that she keeps away. Mula means “root”: this star goes to the foundation of things and tears out what is rotten.

Reads as: Investigates to the root, philosophical, uncompromising. Life tends to strip away false supports. The shadow is destruction for its own sake.

20 · Purva Ashadha पूर्वाषाढा

The Waters of the Rig Veda are mothers, healers and purifiers. They carry no army but they wear down stone, which is the idea of invincibility by persistence.

Reads as: Persuasive, invigorating, undefeated by opposition. The shadow is stubborn pride.

21 · Uttara Ashadha उत्तराषाढा

The Vishvedevas are the assembly of all the gods, invited to every shraddha. This star is the final victory that is earned by dharma rather than by a single patron.

Reads as: Lasting achievement through integrity. Slow to start, hard to defeat. The shadow is rigidity.

Gandanta: Jyeshtha to Mula

Jyeshtha ends where Scorpio ends and Mula begins where Sagittarius begins: water to fire again. The same sensitive-junction idea applies, and the last pada of Jyeshtha and first pada of Mula are the usual caution zone. The Jyotirnibandha, as cited on a muhurta reference page, also rejects the first quarter of Mula for marriage, although Mula is otherwise on the marriage list.

Abhijit sits after this group

{{term:abhijit|abhijit}}, the short 28th nakshatra, belongs between Uttara Ashadha and Shravana. It is a muhurta extra. Its deity is Brahma in the Brihat Samhita.

Where the schools differ

Mula’s deity. The Nakshatra Suktam’s verse names Nirriti, the goddess of decay and dissolution. The Brihat Samhita’s deity table (ch. 98, Iyer’s translation) lists Prajapati for Mula, so both names are old. The idea of “root” (mula) fits either, but Nirriti is the more common choice in Jyotish books.

Symbols. Vishakha is a triumphal arch in most lists and a potter’s wheel in others. Anuradha is a lotus (some say an archway or a staff). Jyeshtha is a circular amulet, an earring or an umbrella. Purva and Uttara Ashadha both use a tusk in some lists, a fan or planks of a bed in others.

Vishakha’s name. Some call it Radha. “Anuradha” literally means “following Radha”, so the two names are linked in the tradition.

Cross-check

The Moon’s nakshatra on any day is easy to cross-check with a panchang. The Moon at Swati to Uttara Ashadha spans roughly Libra to Sagittarius to early Capricorn. Look at a free panchang for a week in a Libra or Scorpio Moon, note the nakshatras, then check them against these spans. They should match exactly (Lahiri).

  • Swati (Rahu, Vayu) and Vishakha (Jupiter, Indra-Agni) are Movable and Mixed; Anuradha (Saturn, Mitra) is Soft and Deva.
  • Jyeshtha and Mula are two of the four Sharp nakshatras; they bracket the second gandanta junction.
  • Mula’s deity: Nirriti (common) or Prajapati (some lists).
  • Purva Ashadha is Fierce, Uttara Ashadha Fixed and marriage-friendly.

The nakshatras one by one

22 · Shravana श्रवण

Vishnu took three strides across the cosmos as Vamana, the dwarf, to win it back from Bali. Shravana means “hearing”: the star of listening, learning and the teaching that is passed by ear.

Reads as: Learning by listening, connecting people and traditions. Fame can come through speaking or teaching. The shadow is gossip and over-reliance on what others say.

23 · Dhanishta धनिष्ठा

The Vasus are eight elemental gods of fire, earth, wind, sky and so on. In the Mahabharata one Vasu, cursed to be born as a human, becomes Bhishma, the lifelong vow-keeper. The listed names of the eight vary by text.

Reads as: Rhythm, wealth, ambition and group success. Music and timing are strengths. The shadow is a hard, acquisitive streak.

24 · Shatabhisha शतभिषा

Varuna is lord of the cosmic waters and of rita, the moral order. “Hundred physicians” points to the herbs and rites by which he heals and binds.

Reads as: Healing, research, secrecy and solitude. A mind that works alone. The shadow is isolation and hidden pain.

25 · Purva Bhadrapada पूर्वभाद्रपदा

Aja Ekapada, “the one-footed unborn”, is a Vedic storm and sun god who props up the sky on one foot. He is linked to Rudra and to the fire of sacrifice.

Reads as: Intensity, idealism and a fierce drive that can burn through the old. The shadow is extremes and a two-faced life.

26 · Uttara Bhadrapada उत्तरभाद्रपदा

Ahirbudhnya, “the serpent of the deep”, lives in the cosmic waters, a guardian of what lies at the bottom of the sea. The rain he brings is the slow, soaking kind.

Reads as: Depth, calm, endurance and wisdom. Good at long, quiet work. The shadow is withdrawal and over-caution.

27 · Revati रेवती

Pushan is shepherd of the roads and guide of travellers and herds. At Daksha’s sacrifice his teeth were knocked out, so he is shown eating soft food. The last star of the zodiac guides the journey home.

Reads as: Gentle, protective and nourishing, a guide for others’ journeys. The shadow is over-giving and difficulty ending things.

Gandanta: Revati to Ashwini

Revati ends where Pisces ends and Ashwini begins where Aries begins. This is the third water-to-fire junction and the one that closes the zodiac wheel. The last pada of Revati and the first pada of Ashwini are the caution zone. The Jyotirnibandha, as cited on a muhurta reference page, also rejects the last quarter of Revati for marriage.

Where the schools differ

The Vasus. Dhanishta’s deity is the eight Vasus. Texts do not list the same eight names: the Mahabharata, the Puranas and the Vedic texts differ. The count of eight is stable.

Bhadrapada deities. Aja Ekapada and Ahirbudhnya are Vedic names, often treated as forms of Rudra. Some reference sites render them as one-footed and “serpent of the deep” forms of Rudra. Jyotish tables mostly agree on the names themselves.

Symbols. Both Bhadrapadas are shown as legs of a funeral cot (front and back), though in some lists Purva Bhadrapada is a two-faced man or swords and Uttara Bhadrapada is twins. Revati is a fish in most lists, a drum in some. Dhanishta is a drum or a flute.

Cross-check

The last six nakshatras end the zodiac, so they give an arithmetic check: Shravana starts at 280° (Capricorn 10°) and Revati ends at 360°. Compute the start of each of the six as (number − 1) × 13°20′, then compare with the span column. Then re-run your Jupiter with another ayanamsa to see how a planet near an edge changes nakshatra.

In your chart

Two of your planets sit in this group of six:

PlanetPlacementStar lordD9 (from the pada)
JupiterPisces 3°28′, Uttara Bhadrapada pada 1SaturnLeo
KetuAquarius 10°33′, Shatabhisha pada 2RahuCapricorn

Jupiter is only 8′ past the start of Uttara Bhadrapada (Pisces 3°20′), the boundary with Purva Bhadrapada. Under Lahiri, KP and Raman ayanamsas it stays in Uttara Bhadrapada (3°28′, 3°34′, 4°55′), but under Fagan-Bradley it falls to Pisces 2°35′, in Purva Bhadrapada. Ketu in Shatabhisha is in Rahu’s nakshatra, and your Rahu is in Ketu’s nakshatra, Magha. The nodes sit in each other’s stars.

Remember
  • Shravana (Moon, Vishnu), Dhanishta (Mars, Vasus) and Shatabhisha (Rahu, Varuna) are all Movable.
  • Purva Bhadrapada is Fierce (Jupiter), Uttara Bhadrapada Fixed (Saturn), Revati Soft (Mercury).
  • Revati is the last nakshatra and, with Ashwini, forms the third gandanta junction.
  • Your Jupiter is only 8′ past the Purva/Uttara Bhadrapada boundary; boundaries depend on the ayanamsa.

Practice: for your Jupiter and Ketu, write the nakshatra, pada, lord and D9 sign from the rules, then list which of the other planets also sit in a nakshatra ruled by Saturn or by the nodes.
lessons.listen: Six nakshatras from Shravana to Revati, the end of the zodiac. Shravana, ruled by the Moon, deity Vishnu, is the ear and the three footprints, Movable. Dhanishta, ruled by Mars, deity the eight Vasus, is the drum, Movable and Rakshasa gana. Shatabhisha, ruled by Rahu, deity Varuna, is the empty circle and the hundred physicians. Purva Bhadrapada, ruled by Jupiter, deity Aja Ekapada, is Fierce. Uttara Bhadrapada, ruled by Saturn, deity Ahirbudhnya, is Fixed, depth and endurance. Revati, ruled by Mercury, deity Pushan, the guide of travellers, is Soft, the last nakshatra. Between Revati and Ashwini is the third gandanta junction. Your Jupiter is in Uttara Bhadrapada pada one, only eight arcminutes past the boundary, and your Ketu is in Shatabhisha pada two.

lessons.title: Tara bala, Chandra bala and the link to matching
lessons.body:
Recall: Which nakshatra do you count as 1 for your tara bala, and what tara is the nakshatra that follows it?

You can now read any nakshatra. This lesson builds {{term:tarabala|tara bala}} and {{term:chandrabala|chandra bala}} from the Moon’s daily nakshatra and sign against your own birth Moon to produce two quick day filters. They belong to {{term:muhurta|muhurta}}, the art of choosing times, not to prediction of events. Treat them as one filter among several, never as a verdict on a day.

Tara bala: nine taras

StepRuleExample (your Pushya, Moon in Chitra)
1. CountFrom your birth nakshatra (counted as 1) to the Moon’s nakshatra today, inclusivePushya 1, Ashlesha 2, Magha 3, Purva Phalguni 4, Uttara Phalguni 5, Hasta 6, Chitra 7
2. DivideDivide the count by 9 and keep the remainder (0 counts as 9)7 ÷ 9 = 0 remainder 7
3. ReadThe remainder is the taraRemainder 7 is Naidhana, the worst
RemainderTaraMeaningVerdict
1Janma (birth)The birth star itselfMixed: avoid important new starts in the first cycle
2SampatWealthGood
3VipatDangerBad
4KshemaWell-beingGood
5Pratyak (or Pratyari)ObstacleBad
6Sadhana (Sadhaka)AchievementGood
7Naidhana (Vadha)Harm, endingWorst: avoid
8MitraFriendGood
9 (or 0)Param Mitra (Atimitra)Great friendBest

Because 27 = 3 × 9, the nine taras repeat three times through the 27 nakshatras. Here is the full table for your birth nakshatra Pushya:

TaraCountsCycle 1Cycle 2Cycle 3
Janma1, 10, 19PushyaAnuradhaUttara Bhadrapada
Sampat2, 11, 20AshleshaJyeshthaRevati
Vipat3, 12, 21MaghaMulaAshwini

Pratyak5, 14, 23Uttara PhalguniUttara AshadhaKrittika
Sadhana6, 15, 24HastaShravanaRohini
Naidhana7, 16, 25ChitraDhanishtaMrigashira
Mitra8, 17, 26SwatiShatabhishaArdra
Param Mitra9, 18, 27VishakhaPurva BhadrapadaPunarvasu

Notice the extra Janma stars: Anuradha (10th from Pushya) and Uttara Bhadrapada (19th). Some traditions call these the Anujanma and Trijanma stars and treat them with some caution, though not as strongly as the birth star itself.

Chandra bala: the Moon’s sign from your Moon

{{term:chandrabala|Chandra bala}} counts the sign of the Moon today from your natal Moon sign (counted as 1). Your Moon sign is Cancer.

House from your MoonSign for youVerdict
1CancerFavourable
2LeoCaution or neutral (varies)
3VirgoFavourable
4LibraUnfavourable
5ScorpioCaution or neutral (varies)
6SagittariusFavourable
7CapricornFavourable
8AquariusUnfavourable (Chandrashtama)
9PiscesCaution or neutral (varies)
10AriesFavourable
11TaurusFavourable
12GeminiUnfavourable

The 8th house, here Aquarius, is {{term:chandrashtama|Chandrashtama}}. The Moon is in it for about two and a quarter days a month. Panchang makers list the Moon’s sign for each day, so you can scan for it.

Using both together

Run both checks on the Moon’s position at the time you plan to act. The engine’s day table prints both for your chart. Sample lines (9 am and 6 pm, Satna time, Moon sign counted from your Cancer):

Date and timeMoon todayHouse from your MoonTaraReading
Sat 28 Nov, 9 amPunarvasu1 (Cancer)Param MitraBoth favourable

Mon 30 Nov, 6 pmMagha2 (Leo)VipatTara bad, Chandra caution: wait
Tue 15 Dec, 9 amDhanishta8 (Aquarius)NaidhanaChandrashtama and worst tara: avoid new starts
Wed 16 Dec, 6 pmPurva Bhadrapada8 (Aquarius)Param MitraGood tara, but Chandrashtama still applies
Thu 17 Dec, 6 pmUttara Bhadrapada9 (Pisces)Janma (3rd cycle)Chandra caution; Trijanma star

Where nakshatras feed matching

Four of the eight kootas of the 36-point Ashtakoota method come straight from the Moon’s nakshatra: Tara (3), Yoni (4), Gana (6) and Nadi (8). That is 21 of the 36 points. Tara koota counts both ways between two birth stars, using the same nine taras. The full method, with its tables and its cancellations, is in the matching stage. For now it is enough to know that the attribute columns you met in lessons 3-2 to 3-5 are the data that matching uses.

Where the schools differ

Janma tara. Many panchangs list Janma as unfavourable, others as mixed. Regional practice differs, and some count only the first cycle as strongly adverse.

Tara names. Pratyak and Pratyari are the same fifth tara; Naidhana and Vadha are the same seventh; Param Mitra and Atimitra the same ninth. Spelling varies, the numbering does not.

Chandra bala houses. The common muhurta rule treats the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th houses from the natal Moon as favourable and the 4th, 8th and 12th as unfavourable. The 2nd, 5th and 9th are treated as caution by some panchangs and as acceptable under certain conditions (such as a bright, waxing Moon) by others. The waxing-Moon condition is not confirmed in a primary text here, so treat it as lineage-dependent.

Where to count from. Most muhurta books count Chandra bala from the natal Moon sign. Some also check the Moon’s house from the lagna.

Remedies. Some panchang sites list charity items for a bad tara (jaggery, salt, sesame seeds with gold). They are practices from the tradition, not part of the calculation. This course uses the checks for planning only.

Cross-check

Verify the engine’s day table by hand once. Pick a date, find the Moon’s nakshatra from any Lahiri panchang for the time you choose, count from Pushya, take the remainder mod 9 and look up the tara. Then count the Moon’s sign from Cancer. Compare with the engine’s line for the same hour. The Moon moves about half a degree an hour, so near a nakshatra or sign edge the answer can change within the day: check the hour before and after.

In your chart

Your birth nakshatra is Pushya and your Moon sign is Cancer. Your next Chandrashtama run after today is 15 to 17 Dec 2026 (Moon in Aquarius, per the engine). On the morning of 15 Dec the Moon is also in Dhanishta, your Naidhana tara, so both filters flag the day. By the evening of 17 Dec the Moon has moved to Pisces and Uttara Bhadrapada, your third Janma star.

These filters help you time ordinary choices (signing, travelling, launching). They are not a forecast of what will happen to you. Log what you did on good and bad filter days in your prediction ledger for a month and compare the two lists honestly.

Remember
  • Tara bala: count inclusive from your birth star, remainder mod 9. Bad: 3, 5, 7 (Vipat, Pratyak, Naidhana); Janma is mixed.
  • The taras repeat three times through the 27 nakshatras: your Janma stars are Pushya, Anuradha and Uttara Bhadrapada.
  • Chandra bala: favourable houses 1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11 from the natal Moon sign; 4, 8, 12 unfavourable; 2, 5, 9 vary.
  • Your Chandrashtama is the Moon in Aquarius.
  • Tara, Yoni, Gana and Nadi kootas (3 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 21 of 36 points) come from the Moon’s nakshatra.

Practice: use the engine’s day command for the next ten days with your Moon sign (Cancer) and nakshatra (Pushya). Mark each day as green (both filters good), amber or red. Decide on a small action for a green day and a red day and record the result in your ledger.
lessons.listen: Two daily filters use the Moon of the day against your birth Moon. Tara bala: count from your birth nakshatra, counted as one, to the Moon’s nakshatra today, divide by nine and read the remainder. The nine taras are Janma, Sampat, Vipat, Kshema, Pratyak, Sadhana, Naidhana, Mitra and Param Mitra. Vipat, Pratyak and Naidhana are the unfavourable ones, and Janma is mixed. For your Pushya, the Janma stars are Pushya, Anuradha and Uttara Bhadrapada. Chandra bala counts the sign of the Moon today from your natal Moon sign. Houses one, three, six, seven, ten and eleven are favourable; four, eight and twelve are not. For your Cancer Moon, Aquarius is your Chandrashtama. Panchang practice varies on the second, fifth and ninth houses and on Janma. These are filters for choosing a time, not predictions. Four of the eight Ashtakoota kootas, worth twenty one of thirty six points, come from the Moon’s nakshatra.

lessons.title: The Vimshottari dasha balance at birth
lessons.body:
Recall: How many tara cycles fit in 27 nakshatras, and which tara does count 19 give?

The nakshatra system’s biggest job is to start the {{term:vimshottari|vimshottari}} {{term:dasha|dasha}} clock. Each {{term:mahadasha|mahadasha}} splits into {{term:antardasha|antardashas}}. This lesson computes it from scratch for your Moon and checks it against the engine.

The 120-year system

Nine planets share 120 years. They follow the nakshatra-lord order, so the lord of your Moon’s nakshatra rules the first dasha.

LordYearsNakshatras it rules
Ketu7Ashwini, Magha, Mula
Venus20Bharani, Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha
Sun6Krittika, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha
Moon10Rohini, Hasta, Shravana
Mars7Mrigashira, Chitra, Dhanishta
Rahu18Ardra, Swati, Shatabhisha
Jupiter16Punarvasu, Vishakha, Purva Bhadrapada
Saturn19Pushya, Anuradha, Uttara Bhadrapada
Mercury17Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, Revati

7 + 20 + 6 + 10 + 7 + 18 + 16 + 19 + 17 = 120.

The idea in one sentence

At birth, the fraction of the Moon’s nakshatra already crossed equals the fraction of that lord’s dasha already used. What is left is the {{term:bhogya|dasha balance}}.

The computation, step by step, on your Moon

StepWorkingResult
1. Moon’s sidereal longitudeEngine: Cancer 8°04′ (98°03′47″ before rounding)98°03′47″
2. Nakshatra and lord98°03′47″ ÷ 13°20′ = 7.35, so the 8th, Pushya. Lord Saturn, 19 yearsPushya, Saturn
3. Start of Pushya7 × 13°20′93°20′00″
4. Elapsed (bhukta)98°03′47″ − 93°20′00″4°43′47″ = 283.8′
5. Fraction elapsed283.8′ ÷ 800′0.3547 (35.5%)
6. Years elapsed19 × 0.35476.74 years
7. Balance (bhogya)19 − 6.74, or 19 × (1 − 0.3547)12.26 years = 12 years 3 months 4 days
8. Dasha start and endBirth 26 Jun 1998 minus 6.74 years; plus 12.26 yearsAbout 29 Sep 1991 to 29 Sep 2010

The engine’s Saturn mahadasha runs 1991-09-29 to 2010-09-29. Your own calculation agrees to the day.

The chain that follows

MahadashaYearsFromTo
Saturn (balance 12.26 years)191991-09-29 (before birth)2010-09-29
Mercury172010-09-292027-09-29
Ketu72027-09-292034-09-29
Venus202034-09-292054-09-29
Sun62054-09-292060-09-29
Moon102060-09-292070-09-29

Today (27 Nov 2026) you are in the Mercury mahadasha, and the engine’s antardasha is Mercury–Saturn, running 2025-01-19 to 2027-09-29. Your next mahadasha, Ketu, starts on 2027-09-29.

The antardasha at birth

Each mahadasha divides among all nine planets in proportion to years, beginning with its own lord: antardasha length (years) = MD years × AD years ÷ 120. For Saturn’s 19 years:

Saturn antardashaLength (years)Engine dates
Saturn–Saturn3.011991-09-29 to 1994-10-02
Saturn–Mercury2.69to 1997-06-11
Saturn–Ketu1.11to 1998-07-21 (you were born here)
Saturn–Venus3.17to 2001-09-20
Saturn–Sun0.95to 2002-09-02
Saturn–Moon1.58to 2004-04-02
Saturn–Mars1.11to 2005-05-12
Saturn–Rahu2.85to 2008-03-18
Saturn–Jupiter2.53to 2010-09-29

Cumulative: 3.01 + 2.69 = 5.70, then + 1.11 = 6.81. You were 6.74 years into Saturn at birth, which falls inside Saturn–Ketu (5.70 to 6.81). Your birth was about 0.07 years, roughly 25 days, before the end of that sub-period.

How sensitive is the balance?

Saturn’s 19 years spread over 13°20′, so each degree of the Moon is worth 19 ÷ 13.33 = 1.43 years of balance, and each arcminute about 9 days. Five minutes of birth time moves the Moon about 3′ and the balance by about 24 days.

Where the schools differ

Length of the year. The engine and most software count a dasha year as 365.25 days. Some traditional calculators and an option in JHora use a 360-day year (the savana year). For your Saturn balance of 12.26 years, the 360-day year would end the Saturn dasha about 64 days earlier, in late July 2010 instead of late September. The ratios are the same; the calendar dates differ.

Which dasha system. Vimshottari is the most widely used dasha in the Parashari tradition (BPHS treats it as the general-purpose dasha and describes other systems with conditions). Other nakshatra-based systems exist: Ashtottari (108 years) and Yogini (36 years) are often used under conditions, and they start from the Moon’s nakshatra in other ways. Compare them only once you know Vimshottari well.

Accuracy of the Moon. The method is exact arithmetic on the Moon’s position. Every difference in dates comes from the ayanamsa, the true or mean calendar year, and the birth time.

Cross-check

Three independent tests of your balance:

TestMoonPadaSaturn balance
Lahiri (this course, engine)Cancer 8°04′Pushya 212.26 years
Birth time 12:54 (−5 min)Cancer 8°01′Pushya 212.33 years
Birth time 13:04 (+5 min)Cancer 8°07′Pushya 212.19 years
Krishnamurti (KP) ayanamsaCancer 8°10′Pushya 212.12 years
Raman ayanamsaCancer 9°31′Pushya 210.20 years
Fagan-Bradley ayanamsaCancer 7°11′Pushya 213.52 years
Yukteshwar ayanamsaCancer 9°26′Pushya 210.30 years

All the systems keep your Moon in Pushya pada 2, so the first dasha lord is Saturn everywhere. But the balance ranges from 10.2 to 13.5 years. Under Raman’s ayanamsa your Mercury dasha would begin about two years earlier, around September 2008 instead of September 2010. This is why a stored convention profile matters: every date in a reading depends on the ayanamsa and year length you chose.

In your chart

Your Moon at Cancer 8°04′ is 35.5% through Pushya, so you were born with 12.26 years of Saturn dasha remaining, and the dasha began on 29 Sep 1991. Saturn ended on 29 Sep 2010 and Mercury began. Mercury runs to 29 Sep 2027, then Ketu to 29 Sep 2034, then Venus (the longest, 20 years) to 29 Sep 2054. The engine’s output agrees with each step above.

Remember
  • Fraction of the nakshatra crossed = fraction of the lord’s dasha used.
  • Balance = lord’s years × (800′ − elapsed′) ÷ 800′.
  • Total 120 years, order Ketu, Venus, Sun, Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury.
  • Your balance: Saturn, 12.26 years, ending 29 Sep 2010; you were born in Saturn–Ketu.
  • Dates move with the ayanamsa (here from −2.1 to +1.3 years across six ayanamsas), the year length (about 64 days over 12 years) and the birth time (about 5 days per minute).

Practice: without looking at the engine, compute the balance for a Moon at Taurus 3°20′ (33°20′, sidereal), then for your own Moon with the ayanamsa set to Raman (Cancer 9°31′). Check your first answer against the quiz, and the second against the cross-check table.
lessons.listen: The Vimshottari dasha gives the nine planets one hundred and twenty years in the nakshatra lord order: Ketu seven, Venus twenty, Sun six, Moon ten, Mars seven, Rahu eighteen, Jupiter sixteen, Saturn nineteen, Mercury seventeen. The Moon’s nakshatra at birth gives the first lord. The fraction of the nakshatra already crossed is the fraction of that dasha already used. Your Moon at ninety eight degrees three minutes forty seven seconds is four degrees forty three minutes into Pushya, which is thirty five and a half percent. Saturn’s nineteen years times thirty five and a half percent is six point seven four years used, leaving twelve point two six. Your Saturn dasha ran from September 1991 to September 2010, then Mercury to September 2027, then Ketu. At birth you were in Saturn Ketu. Dates shift by up to three years with the ayanamsa, about two months with a three hundred sixty day year, and about five days per minute of birth time.

Jagannatha Hora documentation, dasha year options
Vimshottari dasha computed with the app's chart engine (365.25-day year, Lahiri ayanamsa)

quiz.w: 33°20′ ÷ 13°20′ = 2.5, so the 3rd nakshatra, Krittika (lord Sun, 6 years), exactly half crossed. Balance = 6 × 0.5 = 3 years.

quiz.w: The fraction elapsed in the nakshatra equals the fraction of the dasha elapsed. 100% − 35.5% = 64.5% remains.

quiz.q: How many years does the Saturn mahadasha last, and which dasha follows it?
quiz.w: Saturn has 19 years. The order is Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu, so Mercury follows.

quiz.q: A mahadasha of 19 years splits into antardashas. How long is Saturn–Mercury?
quiz.w: MD years × AD years ÷ 120 = 19 × 17 ÷ 120 = 2.69.

o: Raman uses a different dasha order for stars
The Moon sits further along Pushya, so more is crossed
Pushya has a different lord under Raman
Raman adds Abhijit as a 28th nakshatra and shifts the count
quiz.w: Raman puts the Moon at Cancer 9°31′, so 6.2° of Pushya is crossed instead of 4.7°. The balance falls to 10.2 years.

Where the schools differ

Star lord as a rule. Many Parashari teachers use the nakshatra lord as a secondary lens on a planet. KP astrology goes further and makes the star lord (and a sub-lord inside each nakshatra) the decisive factor. Jaimini astrology does not use nakshatras in its core sign-based methods (chara karakas, arudhas, chara dasha). These are different weights on the same data.

Cross-check

Run the same reading with two separate systems. Check your nakshatra table against a free chart cast with Lahiri ayanamsa. Then check the dasha chain against a different software’s Vimshottari output with the 365.25-day year. Differences of a few days are normal; differences of a year mean the ayanamsa or the birth time differs.
